# Runs A, B and C: membership validation stops before any worktree exists

All three runs stop at checklist step 2, before the worktrees are set up. The legs reference requires every selected sibling to pass validation before any tree is created. In each run, repo-b fails that check. As a result, none of the runs reaches step 4. Each run's first message to the user is the blocking stop below, and **no run produces an approaches message**.

The steps before the stop are the same in all three runs:

- Membership is decided by matching identifiers before any filesystem or git probe. The ask explicitly selects repo-b. That matches the home `## shape-ticket` declaration `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` by `NAME` and by `owner/name` (`acme/repo-b`). The companion primary is `/work/repo-b`.
- repo-c is declared but not selected. It is never probed, so its missing checkout is never observed. It is not a stop condition and is not mentioned to the user.
- No trees exist yet, so there is nothing to preserve or list.

---

## Run A: PATH missing

**(1) First message**

> Blocking stop: the brainstorm can't set up worktrees. The selected companion repo-b is declared in `/work/repo-a`'s overrides under `## shape-ticket` as `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git`. That resolves to `/work/repo-b`, which does not exist.
>
> I validate every selected companion before creating any worktree, so nothing has been created. No worktrees exist for repo-a or repo-b.
>
> To continue, clone repo-b to `/work/repo-b`, or fix or remove that sibling line. Then restart.

**(2) Approaches message:** none. Step 4 is not reached.

---

## Run B: PATH is the home checkout

**(1) First message**

> Blocking stop: the brainstorm can't set up worktrees. The selected companion repo-b is declared under `## shape-ticket` as `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git`. Its path `/work/repo-b` is a symlink, and once resolved it points to `/work/repo-a`, the home checkout itself. A companion can't be the home repo.
>
> I stopped before probing its origin and before creating any worktree. No worktrees exist.
>
> To continue, replace the symlink with a real repo-b clone at `/work/repo-b`, or fix that sibling line. Then restart.

**(2) Approaches message:** none. Step 4 is not reached.

---

## Run C: PATH is not a checkout

**(1) First message**

> Blocking stop: the brainstorm can't set up worktrees. The selected companion repo-b is declared under `## shape-ticket` as `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git`. Its path `/work/repo-b` exists but is not a git checkout, so I can't read or verify its origin.
>
> No worktree was created for either repo.
>
> To continue, make `/work/repo-b` a clone of `git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git`, or fix that sibling line. Then restart.

**(2) Approaches message:** none. Step 4 is not reached.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
### Run A — selected sibling path missing
1. Match the explicitly selected `repo-b` to `git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` before filesystem or Git probes.
2. Check its declared primary path, `/work/repo-b`. The supplied observation says it does not exist.
3. **Stop:** the selected sibling declaration is invalid because its primary path is missing. Create no worktree.

### Run B — selected sibling resolves to home
1. Match the explicitly selected `repo-b` to its declaration before probing.
2. Canonicalize `/work/repo-b` for the home-path comparison. The supplied observation says it symlinks to `/work/repo-a`.
3. **Stop:** the selected companion primary resolves to the home primary. Create no worktree.

### Run C — selected sibling is not a checkout
1. Match the explicitly selected `repo-b` to its declaration before probing.
2. Check `/work/repo-b`. The supplied observations say it exists but is not a Git repository.
3. **Stop:** the selected sibling primary is not a checkout. Create no worktree.

In every run, **preserved created legs: none**. Do not probe `repo-c`: it was not selected, so its missing checkout is irrelevant. These validation failures block progress before worktree creation, questionary, or approaches.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs satisfy the fact: each of A/B/C stops at step 2 before any worktree creation (home included), quotes the selected `- sibling: git@github.com:acme/repo-b.git` declaration, names the missing / equal-home / non-repository cause, resolves B's symlink to `/work/repo-a` before comparing it to home, and explicitly states repo-c is unselected, never probed, and not mentioned to the user. After is slightly more explicit than Before (it adds that B stopped before probing origin and gives the overrides location in A), so nothing moved; if the author expected a fails->holds movement here, the baseline already held, and the current After wording can be kept as-is — the only optional tightening would be to use the word 'canonicalizes' in Run B rather than 'once resolved it points to', so a strict reader keys on the fact's exact term.
